ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Zora Neale Hurston Synthetic CCD

text.paragraph: Establishing care for morning headaches, breathlessness on exertion and ankle swelling, with very high blood pressure: examination, ECG, laboratory tests, 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring, a two-drug combination, food and medicine-cost screening, and stroke warning signs. Concerns: She wants to keep teaching, writing and gardening, and to get her breath back; She cannot afford expensive medicines or extra trips, and food runs short at the end of the month; She wants her own account of her symptoms to be believed and every choice explained. [S]

tr.td: Twelve-lead electrocardiogram: sinus rhythm at 80 per minute, left ventricular hypertrophy by voltage criteria with repolarization changes, no atrial fibrillation, no Q waves
24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring, fitted at the visit and returned the next morning, before the first doses of blood pressure medicine

Transthoracic echocardiography: ejection fraction 62%, concentric left ventricular hypertrophy (septum 13 mm, posterior wall 12 mm), grade II diastolic dysfunction with average E/e' 15, left atrial volume index 38 mL/m2, tricuspid regurgitation velocity 2.8 m/s, no significant valve disease, no pericardial effusion
Twelve-lead electrocardiogram at the sick visit: sinus rhythm at 96 per minute, left ventricular hypertrophy unchanged from intake, no arrhythmia
Advance care planning conversation, about 20 minutes, with her consent

list.item: Very high blood pressure at intake (178/104 and 174/102 mmHg) with morning headaches for two months, without signs of a hypertensive emergency; not previously diagnosed; ambulatory monitoring to confirm: resolved, confirmed [S]
Breathlessness on exertion for three months (walking to the school, carrying groceries) with mild ankle swelling by evening; cause to be determined: resolved, confirmed [S]

Hypertensive heart disease with heart failure: stage 2 hypertension confirmed by 24-hour ambulatory monitoring (mean 158/96 mmHg, non-dipping at night), with concentric left ventricular hypertrophy on ECG and echocardiogram; synthetic modern episode linked to the hypertensive heart disease recorded as her cause of death: active, confirmed [S]
Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (ejection fraction 62%), NYHA class II, with grade II diastolic dysfunction and an enlarged left atrium: active, confirmed [S]
Food insecurity: food runs short at the end of most months (Hunger Vital Sign positive): active, confirmed [S]
Low and irregular income from substitute teaching and newspaper writing, with Original Medicare but no drug coverage; medicine costs a barrier: active, confirmed [S]

Orthostatic hypotension with lightheadedness on standing, from volume depletion in early summer heat on a diuretic, spironolactone and an SGLT2 inhibitor; no fall or faint; resolved after two days off those medicines and more fluid: resolved, confirmed [S]

list.item: Writer, folklorist and anthropologist trained at Barnard; now works as a substitute teacher at the local high school and writes a weekly newspaper column; working on a new book [S]
Lives alone in a small house in Fort Pierce that a friend from her hometown lets her live in without rent; keeps a garden and a dog; no car, walks or takes the bus; no air conditioning, only fans [S]

Income: daily substitute-teaching pay when called and small payments for her column, plus a small Social Security benefit; book royalties have been small; Original Medicare (Part A and Part B) with no drug plan and no supplemental coverage, because she could not afford the premiums [S]
Diet: home cooking with salt pork, greens, rice, fish and cornbread; canned foods at the end of the month when money runs short; adds salt at the table [S]
Tobacco: never. Alcohol: rarely, a glass at a celebration. No drug use [S]

Strengths and supports: raised in Eatonville, an all-Black town she calls home; a lifelong collector of stories; describes a wide circle of friends, students and neighbors, and a sense of humor she relies on [S]
Says she has often had to insist on being taken seriously, and asks that her account of her own body be believed and that every choice be explained to her as to a colleague [S]

tr.td: Establishing care for morning headaches, breathlessness on exertion and ankle swelling, with very high blood pressure: examination, ECG, laboratory tests, 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring, a two-drug combination, food and medicine-cost screening, and stroke warning signs
Two-week review: ambulatory blood pressure result, echocardiogram, metabolic panel, cardiology consultation the same day, and the diagnosis
Two-week review after dapagliflozin: metabolic panel, blood pressure and potassium, and benefits applications
Eight-week review: blood pressure at home and in the clinic, potassium and kidney function, lipids, KCCQ-12 and drug coverage
Seven-month review: blood pressure, heart failure status, metabolic panel, stroke prevention and plans for the year
Same-day sick visit for lightheadedness on standing in the heat
Respectful, shared decision-making: take her history as given, explain each test and medicine with its reasons and alternatives, write the plan down, and check costs with her before prescribing

Cardiology consultation on the day of the two-week visit, with the echocardiogram, to confirm the cause of breathlessness, look for hypertensive heart disease and HFpEF and their mimics, and advise on treatment

Confirm the diagnosis with 24-hour ambulatory blood pressure monitoring today, before the first dose; then home readings twice daily with a validated upper-arm monitor and a large cuff lent by the clinic

Start a two-drug combination for stage 2 hypertension: chlorthalidone 12.5 mg and amlodipine 5 mg every morning, from the morning after the ambulatory monitor is removed, as low-cost generics; target below 130/80 mmHg; less salt, using foods she already eats

Baseline tests: ECG, NT-proBNP, metabolic panel and magnesium, hemoglobin, TSH, hemoglobin A1c, lipids, ALT and urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio; echocardiogram because of raised NT-proBNP, breathlessness and suspected left ventricular hypertrophy
Stroke and emergency warning signs: BE FAST (balance, eyes, face, arm, speech, time to call 911), and call 911 for chest pain, severe headache with confusion or vision loss, or breathlessness at rest

Costs and coverage, with the clinic's community health worker: a SHINE counselor for Extra Help and the Medicare Savings Program; generic medicines in 90-day fills; patient assistance for any brand-only medicine until coverage begins
Food: the Hunger Vital Sign at intake; help applying for SNAP through ACCESS Florida; the food pantry list

Heart failure treatment: dapagliflozin 10 mg daily with sick-day rules; daily weights with a written plan; metabolic panel one to two weeks after each start or dose change, then every three to six months; KCCQ-12 every three to six months
Atorvastatin 20 mg daily for primary prevention, with a lipid panel at four to twelve weeks
Add spironolactone 12.5 mg daily for blood pressure above target and low potassium on chlorthalidone; potassium and creatinine one to two weeks later
Laboratory checks on the day of clinic visits where possible, and rides through the county's transportation program for people without a car when a separate trip is needed
Heat plan for the Florida summer: fans and cooling places, water through the day, sick-day rules for chlorthalidone, spironolactone and dapagliflozin, and the energy assistance program's cooling help
Blood pressure below 130/80 mmHg in the clinic and at home within six months
Breathlessness only on heavy exertion and a KCCQ-12 score at least 15 points higher within six months
KCCQ-12 54 to 78; NYHA class I to II; ankles no longer swell
Every medicine affordable: generic 90-day fills, patient assistance until drug coverage begins, Extra Help and the Medicare Savings Program
Extra Help and the Medicare Savings Program approved; enrolled in a drug plan; dapagliflozin by patient assistance until then
SNAP approved and the food pantry at her church; food lasts the month
Know the BE FAST signs of stroke and call 911 at once if any appear
She teaches back the signs and keeps the card by the telephone

list.item: Independent in all daily activities; breathless after one flight of stairs or a block carrying groceries; stands for long school days with swollen ankles by evening; NYHA class II [S]
Alert, witty and exact in her history; frustrated that tiredness is slowing her writing; mood steady; PHQ-2 score 1 [S]
